title: Capability registry
description:
Dotted capability ids advertised in the `hello` handshake.

This is the same vocabulary as `spec.capabilities` in plugin.yaml — keystone's manifest schema describes its own field as "identical to the sidecar v1 hello handshake". Keeping one definition means the manifest and the handshake cannot drift: a plugin that declares a capability it does not implement fails at install time rather than at 3am.

The pattern is authoritative and the enum is advisory, for the same reason as error codes: a plugin may advertise capabilities the core has never heard of, and the core simply will not use them.

capabilityId.description: One dotted capability identifier. The pattern is shared verbatim with plugin.yaml's `spec.capabilities`.

wellKnown.description:
Capabilities the core knows how to take advantage of.

`realtime.state-stream` — the plugin pushes state changes as they happen rather than requiring polling.
`discover.devices` — `discover` returns devices already usable by this transport.
`discover.commissionable` — the plugin can find devices not yet paired to anything. Backs keystone's optional CommissionableDiscoverer port.
`commission.setup-code` — pairing accepts a typed setup code.
`commission.qr-code` — pairing accepts a scanned QR payload.
`commission.permit-join` — pairing is a mode rather than a per-device operation (Zigbee-style).
`camera.webrtc` — the plugin can broker WebRTC signalling for a camera. Backs keystone's optional CameraStreamer port. Signalling only: no media crosses the protocol.
`config.flow` — the plugin implements the `configFlow` wizard rather than only a flat config object.
`config.reload` — `setConfig` is applied without a restart.
`health.detailed` — `getHealth` returns per-component counters, not just an overall status.

capabilityList.description: What a plugin advertises in `hello`. Unknown ids are legal and simply unused by the core.

coreFeature.title: Core-side feature
coreFeature.description:
Advertised by the core in the hello response — what the core itself supports.

`seq.replay` — the core tracks `seq` and will call `resume` after a reconnect. A plugin that sees this must keep its ring buffer.
`topic.filtering` — the core sends `subscribe` filters; a plugin that sees this may drop unmatched pushes before numbering them.

coreFeatureList.description: What the core advertises back in the hello response. Closed enum, unlike plugin capabilities: a plugin must not have to guess what an unknown core feature implies about its own obligations.
